I will keep the year simple and steady. I am 64, my land is only 7 mu, and my household labor is limited, so I will not spread myself too thin with too many complicated practices. Since cotton is my main crop and I have long experience with it, I will put most of my land into cotton. Cotton gives me the crop I know best, and with well irrigation I can hold it through dry periods. I will use improved seed instead of something risky or too expensive, keep fertilizer moderate, irrigate a few key times, and control insects when pressure shows up. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage than deep ploughing every year.

I will keep a smaller part of the land in the wheat and maize chain, with wheat in winter and maize after it in summer on the same 2 mu. I will do that because it spreads risk and gives me grain from land that is already suited to that rotation. Wheat and maize are more familiar and straightforward for me, and I do not need to push for the highest possible input level. I will use hybrid maize for better stand and yield, improved wheat seed for stability, fertilize both at moderate levels, irrigate with my well when the crop most needs it, and keep pesticide use limited to what is necessary. My goal this year is not to chase extremes. I will manage for reliable production, lower labor strain, and fewer chances of losing money.
